Merges with (does not replace) the user-level ~/.claude/settings.json hooks. uv migration (ADR-106, [#432]): python hook commands run `uv run --locked` so they execute in the declared environment (committed uv.lock); the ONE deliberate exception is the ADR-77 PreToolUse guard below, which stays on the system interpreter — it is stdlib-only and fail-closed, and a stale lockfile must never be able to block every Edit/Write call in a session. PreToolUse: the E-29/013-A prompts-dir scope guard (scripts/fleet_health.py --prompts-guard, matcher narrowed off "*" to the filesystem-touching tool classes by [#684]) -- ARMED 2026-09-07 in the same act as the daemon restart, never before: while the two CLAUDE_PROMPTS_DIR scopes disagree it refuses EVERY tool call with no in-session escape (measured 2026-09-06). Rationale and the two-legged design are in that module's wiring comment. [#684] 2026-09-11 -- the command now RESOLVES ITS OWN ROOT: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` prefers the variable and falls back to cwd (hook commands run through a POSIX shell whose cwd is the project dir, measured), and `[ -f "$g" ] || exit 0` makes a guard that cannot be LOADED pass instead of refuse. A SECOND `[ -f ]` attempt at cwd was added 2026-09-11 by the fresh Codex review of this branch (HIGH-1): `:-` defaults only on unset-or-empty, so a variable set to the WRONG root skipped the fallback and fell through to fail-open without consulting a guard that was in cwd all along (measured: old rc=0, new rc=7). Fail-open is now reserved for the case where NO root resolves. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set by Claude Code and by nothing else, so the old bare form turned any other reader honouring this file (cursor-agent, measured over two paid runs) into total refusal of every tool call, presenting as the reader being broken. Nothing the guard guards is weakened -- where the script resolves it runs with full force and a mismatch still exits 2. See docs/audits/2026-09-10-technical-night-aj-m03/REVIEW.md:83 and tests/test_prompts_guard_hook_wiring.py. The MATCHER also narrowed in the same act, off "*" to Read|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Glob|Grep|Bash|PowerShell -- the classes a stale CLAUDE_PROMPTS_DIR actually makes lie. The refusal is NOT narrowed: a mismatch still stops the seat at its first file-touching call, which is the first thing any session does. What the narrowing buys is the break-glass: matcher "*" gated ToolSearch too, and ToolSearch is the only route to the deferred ExitWorktree / SendMessage tools, so the 2026-09-06 wedge could not be undone from inside the session at all (recovery took an external shell). Then the ADR-77 immutability guard (scripts/hooks/block_immutable_edits.py) blocks in-place edits of existing transcripts under docs/decisions/transcripts/** (fail-closed in-zone, fail-open out-of-zone; follows the global block-onedrive template) — refs #105. //autoMode: A2 hardening on the #86 cloud-night envelope (Arc 5, architect-ruled land-now 2026-07-06; source: docs/audits/2026-07-06-changelog-review.md A2). Native auto-mode safety nets: 2.1.178 pre-launch subagent classification + 2.1.183 destructive-git blocks are automatic in auto mode; classifyAllShell (2.1.193) additionally routes ALL Bash/PowerShell through the classifier, not just arbitrary-code-exec patterns. RECONCILIATION vs the deny-first floor (reconcile-or-reject, ruled): RECONCILED as a layered ADDITIVE net — the deny-first floor (PreToolUse guards, platform guards, deny-beats-allow) stays authoritative and is not weakened; these nets fire only in auto-mode contexts (the unattended nightly), can only BLOCK more (never grant), and are inert in the operator's interactive modes. Reinforces core-invariant #3; replaces nothing.
//permissions: Cloud-night safety envelope (platform-guards model; advances #86). Pre-allows the Workflow tool. A2 layer (2026-07-06): see //autoMode — native auto-mode nets harden the unattended path as a complementary layer. RUNTIME REALITY (re-probed 2026-06-04): the native Workflow launcher is NOT enabled in the cloud context (Claude Code on the web / Routines), so the canonical cloud execution path is SPEC-ORCHESTRATION -- the nightly Routine reads .claude/workflows/conformance-hub.js as the canonical SPECIFICATION and executes its three stages via read-only Explore agents (the script's exact stage prompts + schemas; Sonnet verifiers, Opus skeptic/digest). Each nightly run ATTEMPTS the native launcher first and falls back to spec-orchestration -- a free nightly re-probe; the digest reports which path ran, and execution swaps back to native automatically when the platform re-enables it. The Workflow allow is retained for local sessions (where the launcher works) and for that cloud re-enable. NO Write/Edit deny is committed by design: deny beats allow with no path carve-outs, so a blanket deny would break BOTH local daily work and the routine's own digest write. Cloud subagent containment is instead provided by platform guards -- Routines push only to claude/* branches, every run lands in a PR (no auto-merge), the conformance review is read-only by design (schema-bound agents that never write), and the Routine prompt runs a post-run `git status --porcelain` tripwire reported in the PR/digest.
